recipes.name: Harvest Pumpkin Cupcakes
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup Argo® OR Kingsford's® Corn Starch
4 teaspoons Spice Islands® Pumpkin Pie Spice
2 teaspoons Spice Islands® 100% Pure Bourbon Vanilla Extract

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease 32 muffin cups or line cups with paper liners.

Whisk white sugar, pumpkin, eggs, and oil together in a large bowl until evenly blended. Whisk flour, cornstarch, pumpkin pie spice, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together in a separate bowl: beat into pumpkin mixture until well blended.
Divide batter among the prepared muffin cups, filling each ⅔ full.
Bake in the preheated oven until centers spring back when touched, 30 minutes. Cool muffins in the cups for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool, about 25 minutes.

Meanwhile, beat cream cheese and butter together in a bowl with an electric mixer until fluffy. Beat in confectioners’ sugar, orange juice, vanilla extract, and orange zest until smooth. Spread over cooled cupcakes.

raw_recipe.headline: Harvest Pumpkin Cupcakes
raw_recipe.description: A rich and spicy harvest pumpkin cupcake recipe that is quick and easy, featuring an orange cream cheese frosting and only requires 30 minutes to make.

review.reviewBody: Made this for Recipe Group and oh man, are these DELICIOUS!!!!! I maed them exactly as written, and feel no changes are necessary. I got 35 cupcakes out of the recipe and I baked them @ 325 degrees for only 14 minutes (my oven is super HOT). The icing is VERY sweet, but it really compliments the cupcake nicely. I did add a drop of orange oil, just to get a better orange flavor. I was able to ice about 18 cupcakes, but I like a lot of icing, so if you are just gonna spread it on, there should be plenty. I decided to freeze the un-iced cupcakes for another time. I really can't believe how fantastic these turned out...I will be making these many, many more times~YUM! Thanks for sharing. :)

8.7.18 ... https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/215375/harvest-pumpkin-cupcakes/ ... E liked these, had four. :D I went for muffins by reducing sugar to 1 1/2c & didn't fill or frost. I used my pumpkin spice mix (2t cinnamon, 1/2t ginger, 1/4t nutmeg). 'Think more would be okay, but I do like to taste pumpkin in pumpkin recipes; not mostly spices. This made 24 muffins in 30 minutes, perhaps 25 next time. Panko on top before baking is a nice touch & slight crunch.

Here's another five-star review for these delicious cupcakes! The recipe made 24 regular-sized and 8 mini-sized cupcakes for me, and the frosting was spot-on perfect! Another reviewer said hers were done in 22 minutes, so I checked mine at that time, and that was perfect (the minis took a couple of minutes less time). For the frosting, one large orange produced the right amount of zest. It's funny how when I buy any fruit with rind now, I always pick it out with zesting in mind! These are delicious cupcakes! UPDATE: This recipe makes about 75 mini-cupcakes and look perfect using an M1 tip to squish on a dollop of the frosting! Check for doneness at about 15 minutes.

I made these into a pumpkin latte! Made the cake part as indicated. For the foam frosting I cooked 2 egg whites, 3/4 cup sugar, 1/2 tsp clear vanilla extract, and 1/4 cup light corn syrup in a double boiler, stirring constantly for 2 minutes. Remove from heat. Transfer to mixer and whip until stiff peaks. Frost cupcakes. Next I used Chef John's caramel sauce as a drizzle for my latte. So pretty!

This is an excellently moist pumpkin cupcake recipe. However, I must stress that the baking time is extremely wrong; it only takes 20 minutes maximum for these cupcakes! If you were using this recipe to bake an 8", 2 layered cake, then you would bake it around 25-30 minutes. Do not overbake these cupcakes. I also added 2 teaspoons vanilla extract; that's just my thing.

Excellent recipe. I did tweak it, using half brown sugar half white, but that's the only adjustment I made. The recipe made 24 large cupcakes for me. If I had used the large sized pampered chef scoop I'm sure it would have been more like 28-30 but I used a slightly larger scoop which made them puff up above the rim quite a bit. I baked them at 350 in a convection oven for 22 minutes & they came out perfectly.

So yummy!! Everyone loved them. I used a basic cream cheese frosting with a little bit of cinnamon instead of the orange frosting. 1 stick of butter, 1 block of cream cheese, 2 tsp vanilla, 1 tsp cinnamon and 4 cups powdered sugar.

They only needed to bake 20 minutes! They came out perfect. I used a different frosting recipe, my own cream cheese frosting recipe and I added about 1 teaspoon of pumpkin spice. I brought them into work and they were gone within the first few hours. Definitely recommend this cupcake. It was moist, fluffy, and absolutely delicious.

My son asked for a pumpkin cake with chocolate chips for his birthday, so I baked this recipe in 9" layers and added 1 cup of semi-sweet morsels to the dry ingredients. It baked in the same amount of time - 30 mins., although the layers didn't look done, they tested clean. The cake frosted very easily. Was exactly what he was hoping for - we liked it a lot!

Me and my mom LOVED this recipe. We brought it for Thanksgiving and people actually started asking us for recipes! It was divine. The frosting is so silky and smooth. Make sure you bake it for 20-25 minutes, not 30. Our cupcakes finished at 25 minutes. We also added cinnamon on top for a decoration. Definitely recommend for Thanksgiving!

I made these for Recipe Group while I was out of town visiting my son and his family. I put them in the oven just as we were sitting down for dinner. My granddaughter kept on and kept on asking for one, and she really didn't want to wait for the icing. In fact, no one else did either. So everyone had one unfrosted. Later, I made the frosting and iced them. We decided this is actually 2 recipes: a great breakfast muffin with no frosting and a really good frosted cupcake as well. It has 2 completely different tastes. It made 24 cupcakes. ***Update Thanksgiving 2013 - I always have a craft for the grandchildren to do. This year we made turkeys out of this recipe, using a large round blob of chocolate frosting for the body, candy eyes, orange frosting for the beak and legs, and candy corn for the feathers. I still left half of them unfrosted for breakfast muffins. ***Update Aug 2015 - My 88 year old mother remembered these from 2010 and asked me to make her some without the frosting to keep in her freezer for when she wants one for breakfast or snack.
I do not have pumpkin spice so I just doubled the spices on the back of the pumpkin puree can and it was perfect.
Amazing. I did add some meringue powder to my frosting so it would stabilize
We love these cupcakes. My son (age 11) started making these at age 6 & everyone loves them. We don't put the orange zest in but otherwise follow directions exactly. Thank you for sharing.

These were a huge hit! I made them exactly like the recipe said, but baking time for the cupcakes was only around 22 minutes and they were done. The cupcakes are moist and delicious! The icing is something I could sit and eat with a spoon because it’s that good! The hint of orange makes it even better!!! Definitely will make these again and again!

Yum,Yum,Yum! This was by far the best pumpkin cupcake I have ever had! I was craving something yummy to eat so I browsed through the cupcakes and came across this! Just looking at it you know it is going to be good!

I have a funky oven (don’t even ask) so I over baked the first batch. To my pleasant surprise, they still turned out moist and delicious! I got 24 cupcakes out of this recipe. For the frosting I used 2 tsps of orange zest. Plenty of orange flavour and didn’t feel the need to use orange essence. Could’ve used a bit more than 4 cups of icing sugar for better texture but 4 cups was all I had at the mo. These cakes are bloody delicious. Brought them to work for shared morning tea and everyone raved. This recipe is a keeper for sure! Cheers.
Fantastic! These were a big hit!!! I didn't change a thing.
